title: Intake heuristics & sparkline grooming — Sprint 30
content:
Context / goal:
We need a compact, defensible way to triage the growing console intake stream so the backlog we ship into sprint planning has high signal and low noise. This doc captures a lightweight heuristic, a visual wireframe for a per-route 'sparkline' intake dashboard, and a proposed cut/prioritization bucket for Sprint 30 grooming.

Quick summary (TL;DR):
- Introduce a 3-cohort intake classification: Hot / Warm / Cold.
- Surface a 7-day sparkline + delta indicator per route to show recent signal.
- Use a 3-factor score (Impact x Frequency / Effort) to rank items; fast-decisions card actions (defer, schedule, escalate) inline.
- Apply automated pruning rules for Cold cohort older than 90d with low signal.

Why this approach?
- Current intake is noisy: many single-occurrence feature asks and one-off bug reports. Hard to prioritize during sprint planning.
- We need something lightweight (PM+Eng ~10–15m per grooming session) that still surfaces high-value bets.
- Sparkline gives product + SRE a quick visual of momentum.

Heuristic details:
1) Cohort assignment (automated, with manual override)
   - Hot: any item with >3 developer requests or 5 customer mentions in last 14d OR an active Sev1/2 ticket linked.
   - Warm: items with 1–3 developer requests, or 2–4 customer mentions in last 14d, or currently assigned a small spike.
   - Cold: everything else.

2) Signal metric (displayed as sparkline)
   - 7-day sparkline for 'mentions' (internal + customer), with a +/− delta compared to previous 7 days.
   - Supplementary badge: ‘repro rate’ (if linked bug) or ‘request rate’ (if product ask).

3) Scoring (numeric to help sort)
   - Impact (1–5): business/customer impact (PM judgment)
   - Frequency (1–5): how common across customers/internal teams
   - Effort (1–5): rough dev + infra cost estimate (lowest is 1)
   - Score = (Impact * Frequency) / Effort  — sort desc.
   - Tiebreakers: Hot cohort -> older -> dependencies.

Wireframe writeup (Figma refs included)
- Top bar: filters (cohort, tag, owner, region, model-route). Quick search supports Jira key and free-text.
- Main list: compact rows, left-to-right: checkbox | sparkline(7d) with delta | title + one-line summary | cohort badge | score pill | est (days) | quick actions menu (defer/schedule/assign/epic-link)
- Row expand (accordion) shows: reporter + last 3 comments, linked Jiras, related routes, suggested rollout (canary region + fallback), and acceptance criteria template.
- Bulk actions: mark as defer, bulk-assign to epic, export selected to sprint planning csv.
- Mini-preview: small thumbnail of suggested wireframe or mock (click opens figma).

Sample backlog section (cut candidates for Sprint 30 grooming)
- RW-3145 | Route: /console/rollouts | Title: 'persist route-level rollback state' | Cohort: Hot | Impact:5 Frequency:4 Effort:3 | Score:6.67 | Est: 3d | Notes: linked to recent outage (SRE postmortem). Priority: ship in next sprint.
- RW-3189 | Route: /console/intake | Title: 'inline triage quick-actions' | Cohort: Warm | Impact:4 Frequency:3 Effort:2 | Score:6.0 | Est: 2d | Notes: UX wireframe ready, Figma abc123. Candidate for sprint 30 if capacity.
- RW-3212 | Route: /console/analytics | Title: 'route-level cost breakdown' | Cohort: Warm | Impact:4 Frequency:2 Effort:4 | Score:2.0 | Est: 5d | Notes: Dep on infra metrics expose. Consider deferred.
- RW-3301 | Route: /console/local-debug | Title: 'improve error logs for private deploy' | Cohort: Cold | Impact:3 Frequency:1 Effort:2 | Score:1.5 | Est: 1d | Notes: low customer signal, keep as backlog.

Automated pruning rules (proposal)
- If cohort == Cold AND last_mention_date < today - 90d AND no linked active Jira -> auto-archive to "intake-archive" label.
- If item archived and gets a new mention or linked Jira it moves back into Warm.
- Admin override: product leads can mark items Permanent.

Grooming cadence + responsibilities
- Weekly lightweight touchpoint (15m) for the Intake Channel owners: PM + Eng rep (rotating), SRE rep when Hot items surface.
- Monthly deep-groom (45–60m) where we re-score Warm->Hot and decide sprint placements.
- Owner responsibilities: add short acceptance criteria, estimate, and any infra dependencies before monthly deep-groom.

Acceptance criteria for the dashboard features (MVP):
- Sparkline shows last 7d mentions and delta.
- Cohort auto-assign runs nightly for new items.
- Quick actions: defer (with optional reason) and assign-to-epic implemented.
- Bulk export to csv (columns: jira, title, cohort, score, est, labels).

Open questions / edge cases (notes-to-self):
- How do we count "mentions" across Slack threads vs. Jira comments? Proposal: only count mentions that contain a ticket/Jira key or come from #intake channel to avoid double-counting noise. Needs engineering confirmation.
- Should tests for knock-on infra risk be part of the score (risk multiplier)? Might complicate scoring; instead capture as a flag to surface in row-expansion.
- UX: do we autohide Cold cohort by default? PMs prefer focus, Engs want complete visibility. Default to filter to Hot+Warm; allow opt-in for Cold.

Next steps (this sprint):
- Marco: prototype wireframe in Figma using rows/accordions + sparkline component (due 2026-02-24).
- Rae: quick spike to enumerate how many current Cold items are >90d and match the prune rule (Jira query) (due 2026-02-25).
- Jonah: small infra spike to surface 7d mention counts (estimate 2d) and provide endpoint for dashboard (due 2026-03-04).
- Aisha (me): pull Sprint 30 grooming deck and run 15m session with PM/Eng on 2026-03-02 to apply heuristics.

Appendix: short glossary
- Mention: discrete reference in Slack or Jira that ties to intake id.
- Sparkline delta: (sum last 7d - sum prior 7d) / sum prior 7d, capped at +/- 200% for display.
- Permanent: flag to never auto-archive.

Notes to reviewers: please add objections inline. If you disagree with the formula or cohort thresholds, suggest numbers and we can A/B for 4 weeks. This doc is intentionally lightweight — we want fast grooming, not additional process overhead.

-- end --
